Fort William is officially the Outdoor Capital of the UK — the adventure capital, the mountain town, the whole personality. Its gluten-free scene is somewhat less extreme.

Honest numbers: Fort William scored 5/10 on my GF safety scale, my lowest in Scotland, and no restaurant broke 3/5. Quick scale translation, because 3/5 sounds worse than it is: my scores grade celiac safety, not deliciousness. A 3/5 means GF options, staff who get it, and a meal I ate happily. The 5/5s are reserved for dedicated menus and dedicated fryers — the full ceremony.

→ Ben Nevis — the UK's tallest mountain, and the whole reason you're here. The summit was socked in fog when I got there, but on the way down the clouds dropped below the path: Loch Linnhe glittering on one side, Fort William spread out underneath.
→ Browns — the restaurant at the Nevis Bank Inn, tied for best of my Fort William bunch at 3/5. The GF chocolate tart is the headliner — it was INCREDIBLE (which from me is basically a standing ovation).
→ Where I stayed: Nevis Bank Inn — the team packed me a GF lunch for the Ben Nevis hike, which tells you everything about how they look after celiac guests. Booking link is in the guide.
→ The Geographer — 3/5, lively spot on the high street, and the place my guide sends you for GF calamari.

Also in the full guide: three more GF options I researched, including Crannog at Garrison West, the one that got away and top of my list for next time. Plus the Glenfinnan Viaduct (yes, the Harry Potter one — I rode the train right over it and forgot to look out the window, a personal best).

The full Fort William guide — all 5 restaurants with honest GF scores, the hotel, and a map — is on the site (link in bio). Verdict: come for the mountain. If your hotel packs you a GF summit lunch, you've already won.
